newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian lawmakers linked to kidnap-murder case.
newsitem.headline: Colombian lawmakers linked to kidnap-murder case.

text.p: Three politicians from Colombia's southern Caqueta province have been linked t the kidnapping of a former ruling party legislator who was found dead in a Caqueta river in May, authorities said on Friday.

"They're believed to be involved in the case surrounding the kidnapping and death of Rodrigo Turbay," a police official told Reuters. He declined to elaborate but said the members of the provincial congress would be presented to reporters at National Police headquarters in Bogota later in the day.

The Radionet news programme identified the three as Carlos Andres Paez Moreno and Paulo Parra, both of the ruling Liberal Party, and Boris Alberto Cabrera of the leftist Patriotic Union. They were detained early on Friday by undercover police in Florencia, the provincial capital, and bundled aboard a flight to Bogota.

Turbay, 37, a former president of the lower house of Congress, was abducted by Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) rebels in Caqueta in June 1995 and accused of stealing funds from the local government.
In a statement sent to a radio station in Caqueta, the FARC said he drowned on May 3 when the boat in which rebels were moving him from one hideout to another capsized.

Turbay, from an influential family of Caqueta politicians, had been stripped of his Liberal Party seat in Congress shortly before his kidnapping because of his alleged links to known drug traffickers.
